transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE); Liam Patel (CTO, OceanView); Sofia Ramirez (ML Eng); Evelyn Brooks (Ops); Jordan Lee (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick demo of model catalog, discuss which open models to prioritize (Llama-2, Mistral, Falcon variants), go over benchmark numbers and compatibility with A100/H100, review quantization/NG4 (sic), and outline POC steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros from our side, im maya chen i own the account and carlos here is our se who runs most of the perf work
[00:12] Carlos Ortega: hi all, thanks. i'll be walking through the model catalog, compatibility matrix, and some benchmark artifacts we ran on common hardware, also happy to dig into specific latency/cost numbers
[00:20] Liam Patel: great thanks, we are pretty tight on latency for a clinical triage use case. targeting sub-300ms for single-turn responses at P95 for short prompts, and also care a lot about on-prem options because of data residency
[00:34] Sofia Ramirez: and to add, our infra team is evaluating A100s in our colo, but we may also test on AWS p4d and g5 instances. curious how Redwood handles quantized runtimes and if we lose accuracy
[00:46] Carlos Ortega: totally. so overview: the model catalog in the console groups open models by verified performance profiles. you can filter by tokenizer size, sequence length, quantization support, and recommended kernel/hardware. we surface per-model benchmarks for latency, throughput, and per-token cost under different batching policies
[01:05] Maya Chen: i'll share the link to the compatibility spreadsheet after the call, it's our canonical matrix for model vs hardware vs quantization. includes recommended kernel (cuda, cutlass, triton-like notes) and expected perf ranges.
[01:20] Evelyn Brooks: is that a public link or enterprise only? we need it for internal procurement review
[01:26] Maya Chen: it's a customer-only link, we'll share a read-only copy for OceanView.
[01:30] Jordan Lee: quick question, does Redwood auto-fallback between model variants if capacity isn't there? we want graceful degradation for peak loads
[01:38] Carlos Ortega: yes you can set routing policies — latency-first or cost-first. we support automated fallback to cheaper/quantized model variants or to Dedicated pool depending on your policy.
[01:47] Sofia Ramirez: can you show an example benchmark, like Llama-2-13B vs Mistral-7B for our 128-token prompt distribution?
[01:53] Carlos Ortega: absolutely. pulling up our benchmark slide — note these are illustrative: Llama-2-13B fp16 on A100: P50 ~ 40ms per token, P95 ~ 110ms for 128 tokens when single-request, batch size 1; Mistral-7B int8 nf4 on same hardware: P50 ~ 18ms, P95 ~ 55ms. throughput wise Mistral wins for short prompts due to smaller kv cache and attention compute.
[02:25] Liam Patel: those P95 numbers look higher than we'd like. where's the overhead coming from? transformer's kv cache? scheduling?
[02:31] Carlos Ortega: a few sources — kernel launch latency for small batches, tokenizer overhead (if running server-side), and padding inefficiencies. our Optimize toolkit suggests batching patterns and prefix caching to reduce per-token latency; for interactive use you want lower batch sizes + prefix caching enabled
[02:48] Maya Chen: and don't forget model architecture differences — Falcon-40B tends to be heavier but sometimes gives better utility for longer free-form; for short clinical classification, a 7-13B quantized variant can hit your SLO much cheaper
[03:03] Sofia Ramirez: about quantization — you mentioned nf4 and int8 and maybe awq — do you have guidance for when accuracy degrades? we care about hallucination rates and classification accuracy
[03:12] Carlos Ortega: yes — our catalog includes a quality delta metric vs fp16 baseline on typical benchmarks. nf4/int8 with awq tends to be within 1-3% for classification tasks on many open models. we include per-model evals; there are a few models where int4 shows noticeable drop for certain token distributions — those are flagged.
[03:31] Jordan Lee: compatibility matrix — does it include kernel/runtime versioning? e.g., cuBLAS/cuDNN, Triton, or our internal inference engine versions?
[03:39] Carlos Ortega: it lists recommended CUDA driver versions, cuDNN min versions, and whether Triton or our native runtime was used during verification. for on-prem we can run a validation job and produce a report matching your exact kernel versions
[03:50] Liam Patel: can you run a POC on our dataset? we want to test both free-text triage and a few structured classification prompts
[03:56] Maya Chen: yes, that's exactly the next step we proposed — you share sample prompts and about 500 records, we'll run end-to-end POC benchmarks on both hosted and Dedicated configs and provide a detailed latency/cost/quality matrix
[04:08] Sofia Ramirez: preference is to run on our colo A100 first. we have two A100 40GB nodes. also want to see A100 vs H100 differences
[04:16] Carlos Ortega: makes sense. H100 shows better throughput for larger models and big batch workloads; for small interactive prompts differences are smaller but H100's Tensor Cores and newer kernels help quantized int4 paths significantly. we'll include both in the POC runs
[04:29] Maya Chen: sharing artifact note: i'll drop the compatibility matrix link and the public model catalog demo deck in chat after the call
[04:36] [05:00] Carlos Ortega: demoing the model catalog UI — you can filter for models with verified nf4 support, see our 'quality delta' and 'recommended use cases' tags. click into a model page to see sample evals (SQuAD-like, classification sets) and the perf profile; we also expose a compatibility tab listing validated hardware and kernel notes
[05:22] Sofia Ramirez: and the benchmark numbers shown, are they reproducible? what's the variance we should expect when we run locally?
[05:28] Carlos Ortega: we publish mean/std across runs — variance is usually 5-12% depending on system jitter. for best reproducibility we recommend using our docker bundles or the private runtime images and disabling noisy co-tenants on colo machines during testing
[05:44] Liam Patel: cost side — can you walk through how Redwood reports per-token cost and how Dedicated commit changes numbers?
[05:52] Maya Chen: sure. hosted pricing shows on the model page an estimated per-token cost based on our unit economics. Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing — you get lower per-token for steady-state usage and predictable throughput. we'll provide sample pricing for your expected QPS in the follow-up email
[06:09] Evelyn Brooks: procurement will ask about SOC 2, audit logs, and KMS support — do you have paperwork ready?
[06:16] Maya Chen: yes we have SOC 2 and ISO docs. for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and provide audit logs with per-request metadata retention controls. i'll include the security pack in the follow-up
[06:29] Carlos Ortega: quick note on model variants and rollback — the console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks; so if a quantized variant underperforms you can auto-rollback to fp16 or to a different model in the catalog
[06:44] Sofia Ramirez: for the POC, can we test both int8 nf4 and int4 awq so we can compare accuracy vs perf?
[06:51] Carlos Ortega: yes; we'll include int8, int4 awq where supported. for some models int4 isn't available or flagged as experimental. we'll mark those in the matrix
[07:03] Maya Chen: a couple of real-customer anecdotes — one clinic moved from Falcon-40B fp16 to Mistral-7B int8 for short triage prompts and cut per-token costs by ~60% while maintaining accuracy within their tolerance band
[07:20] Liam Patel: nice. any caveats for tokenization/stop sequences across models? sometimes we see different tokenizers lead to weird prompt length impacts
[07:28] Carlos Ortega: yes different tokenizers change token counts and thus cost — the model page has tokenizer info and expected tokens for common clinical prompt templates, we also offer a tokenization previewer in the console
[07:43] [08:00] Sofia Ramirez: can we get a quick look at the API? we need the SDK examples for streaming and function/tool calling
[08:07] Carlos Ortega: sure — here's the snippet: curl call with streaming SSE, SDK examples in python and node, model param examples showing prefilling kv cache, batch size, and quantization flags. (reads code) note: streaming P95 is influenced by your chunk size and network RTT; for sub-300ms you want small chunks and keep client RTT low
[08:34] Jordan Lee: our infra team will want to know the recommended kernel flags for best throughput on A100. are those in the matrix?
[08:41] Carlos Ortega: yes — e.g., use CUDA 12.x with cuBLASLt, specific Triton versions listed; we also publish kernel flags and a recommended docker run command with env flags to maximize occupancy
[08:52] Maya Chen: any blockers so far from your side?
[08:56] Sofia Ramirez: the main blocker is we need to ensure no quality regressions with quantized variants. also procurement wants the compliance pack and pricing numbers
[09:05] Liam Patel: timeline-wise we're trying to have a POC run before the end of Q1 to inform budget cycle in March
[09:11] Maya Chen: that's achievable — we'll prioritize the POC and target results within two weeks of receiving sample prompts and access details
[09:18] Carlos Ortega: final note on compatibility: some older drivers or mismatched CUDA versions can cause kernel selection to fallback to less optimal paths — that's why we run an initial verification job. we will include that as part of the POC so you get a 'golden image' report
[09:33] Evelyn Brooks: thanks, much clearer. procurement will also ask about data retention and logs — do you have retention controls per environment?
[09:41] Maya Chen: yes, hosted default is 30 days but enterprise customers can extend or disable retention; Dedicated and Private allow full control — we'll include the retention policy doc
[09:50] [10:00] Maya Chen: recap and next steps: carlos will share the compatibility matrix and benchmark spreadsheet; i'll send pricing and security docs; customer will provide sample prompts and infra details; we'll schedule the POC kickoff next week
[10:14] Liam Patel: perfect thanks everyone
[10:18] Sofia Ramirez: thanks, talk soon
[10:22] End of transcript
